title: Store the reversal before the terminal hears anything

blocks.text: After Tuesday's deploy, three cardholders called the bank. Their terminals had printed FAILED, and their statements show the purchases charged. The switch restarted twice during the deploy, both times while purchases were timing out. Reconciliation also found a purchase that the journal lists as being reversed, although no reversal for it ever reached the host. And on Wednesday a cardholder was charged for a purchase that the terminal had reported as failed, after the host's approval arrived a minute late.

`TimeoutHandler` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TimeoutHandler.java` decides what happens once a purchase sent upstream has ended. `onAnswer` is written. Write `onNoAnswer` and `onLateAnswer`; the comment on each says what it must achieve. `Db`, at the top of the file, is the switch's database with its journal and its store-and-forward queue. Changes made in a `Tx` become real together when it commits.
The tests make the process die after a chosen step (a commit, or a message to the terminal) and then look at what survived. About 10 lines in total.

cases.says: after a timeout the reversal naming the purchase is queued, the journal says it is being reversed, and the terminal hears FAILED
a decline that arrives after the timeout leaves the reversal, the journal and the terminal as they were
wherever the process dies, a terminal that heard FAILED has its reversal stored
the journal says a purchase is being reversed exactly when its reversal is queued, wherever the process dies
an approval that arrives after the terminal was told FAILED does not withdraw the reversal or change what the terminal was told
an approval that arrives after the timeout is recorded in the journal as a late approval

origin.section: 20.2. An Entry Is Stored Before Anyone Is Told, and Leaves Only When It Is Acknowledged

concepts: A queued reversal leaves only when the receiver answers it; a late approval does not withdraw it.
The reversal is stored, in the same transaction as its journal record, before the terminal is told the purchase failed.
